subject: Art & Design
title: Typography in Brand Identity
description: A quick win: understand Typography in Brand Identity.

hook.text: Imagine a law firm using Comic Sans. Or a children's toy brand using Times New Roman.

buildup.text: Brand typography communicates personality: serif fonts suggest tradition, sans-serif suggests modernity.

discovery.text: Major brands invest in custom typefaces. Apple's San Francisco, Netflix's Sans, Google's Product Sans — all bespoke.

twist.text: Using a free or common font isn't always bad. Millions of brands use Helvetica successfully.

climax.text: A brand's typography system includes primary, secondary, and accent fonts with strict rules for size, weight.

punchline.text: Font choice is voice choice. Your typography speaks before your words do.

quiz.question: Why do major tech brands create custom typefaces?
options: Custom fonts reinforce unique brand identity across all touchpoints
They can't afford to license existing fonts
Standard fonts don't display correctly on screens

details.summary: Typography communicates brand personality before a single word is read. Serif fonts suggest tradition and authority (The New York Times), sans-serifs signal modernity (Google), scripts convey elegance (Cadillac), and custom typefaces create unique ownership of the visual voice.
details.whyItMatters: Typography is the brand's written voice. Choosing the wrong typeface is like speaking in the wrong tone — a luxury brand in Comic Sans or a children's brand in a rigid serif immediately contradicts its intended message.
takeaways: Serifs suggest tradition; sans-serifs signal modernity
Typography communicates personality before words are read
Custom typefaces create unique visual ownership

faq.question: Should brands use custom or existing typefaces?
faq.answer: Large brands increasingly commission custom typefaces for uniqueness and licensing savings. Smaller brands choose carefully from existing fonts. The key is consistency — using one or two typefaces across all materials builds recognition regardless of whether they're custom or existing.

faq.question: Why did so many brands switch to sans-serif logos?
faq.answer: Sans-serif fonts render more clearly on digital screens, especially at small sizes. As brands shifted to mobile-first experiences, legibility became paramount. The trend also reflects a broader cultural move toward minimalism and approachability over traditional authority.
